# Independent audit: global simplex facet restriction obstruction



Source: `candidate 590c17ce38e5cbde`.
Verifier: `supporting computation verify_global_simplex_facet_restriction_obstruction.py`.

**Result: PASS.** The claimed comparison is between GLOBAL maxima, not
just values at a fixed candidate. The proof genuinely permits every
integer tilt in the restricted family, and the unrestricted upper bound
uses a fixed finite cover of every possible center. The exact verifier
was rerun successfully; its quadratic-field order routine and every
assertion were also read.

There is one harmless wording qualification in Section 6: restriction
to a cube copy of a purely integer cap involving only the extra cube
coordinates can be the entire copy, rather than a proper halfspace.
Its mass is the whole copy and satisfies the required lower bound.
The author has been asked to state this case explicitly. It changes
none of the constants or conclusions.

## 1. Actual body, measure, and complete integer base

The two inequalities x1+x2+z1/2<=1 and x1+x2-z1/2<=1, together with
the box and coordinate inequalities, define exactly the displayed body.
Their intersection is bounded, closed, convex, and has nonempty full
ambient interior. Its integer base is precisely
{-1,0,1} times {0,1}^(n-1), and every fiber is a positive triangle.
The finite-fiber Hausdorff dimension is 2. Its H2 measure is exactly
the sum of the ordinary triangle areas, with no ambient-volume
substitution. The three radii in each copy are 1/2,1,1/2, so the mass
is (3/2)V per copy, where V=1/2.

Only d=2,n>=1 is asserted, as is appropriate for an obstruction. No
unclaimed boundary case of OC is being silently inferred.

## 2. All restricted orientations and all tilts

I checked the clipped-square identity directly. If one clipped term
is full, the sum is at least r^2. Otherwise convexity of x_+^2 gives
at least 2(h_+)^2. A full/empty pair with the prescribed sum is always
available by making one raw argument sufficiently large. When the
second bound is smaller, the equal choice is unsaturated and attains
it. This handles negative thresholds and arbitrary large tilts.

For x_i>=candidate_i, the two endpoint remaining lengths have sum
1-2candidate_i, yielding the exact A formula. For x1+x2<=s, the two
endpoint thresholds have sum 2s, yielding B. Neither computation
restricts the integer coefficient; it ranges over all real values.

A is strictly decreasing and B strictly increasing. The equations
A(t)=B(2t)=U therefore force x1=x2=t at any middle point whose three
listed restricted minima are all at least U. In particular a value
strictly above U anywhere is impossible. This is a global upper
bound, and not a symmetry assumption about a putative maximizer.

At (0,t,t), I separately checked the other orientations:

* For x_i<=t, an endpoint full/empty pair achieves 1/4. If neither is
  full, both raw thresholds are nonnegative and the sum of retained
  areas is at least r(q1+q2)>r^2. If a threshold is negative the other
  is full. Thus the asserted endpoint infimum is exact.
* The negative-coordinate margin over U is t(2-5t)>0.
* For x1+x2>=2t both endpoints can be empty at zero tilt. Its own
  mass is 1-4t^2, whose margin over U is 3/4-8t^2>0.
* Every pure integer cap containing base zero contains the middle
  fiber and at least one endpoint, giving at least 5V/4.

These are all six facet orientations plus the pure integer case.
A containing cap can be shifted to the candidate without increasing
its mass, so through-point computations suffice.

At each extreme base the three displayed isolating facet caps cover
its whole continuous plane and each has mass V/9. Their restrictions
to the other fibers are strictly empty. For example the left positive
coordinate cap has threshold 1/6 and left remaining length 1/3; at
the middle fiber its left side is at most zero. The left negative
sum cap has threshold -1/3, whereas at the middle its left side is
at most -1. The right isolates are the reflected versions. Endpoint
points therefore cannot compete with the middle value U V.

## 3. Exact constants and the GLOBAL unrestricted upper bound

The positive root is t=(sqrt(21)-4)/2, and
t^2+4t=5/4 gives U=4t^2+1/4=(149-32sqrt(21))/4.
The rational bounds in the source are correctly ordered.

For the three new middle caps, the positive weights 1,4/5,9/10
annihilate their continuous normals and their weighted thresholds
equal zero EXACTLY. At base zero their weighted margin is identically
zero throughout the plane. Hence the three CLOSED caps cover every
middle point, with no exceptional boundary points. The third cap's
integer coefficient does not affect this argument on the middle plane.

The one-vertex triangle area formula used for H1 is valid in every
one of its three fibers: the threshold is strictly between the
second-largest and largest vertex values. H2 has the two positive
endpoint lengths shown in the source. H3 has threshold zero at the
left endpoint, s at the middle, and 2s>1/2 at the right endpoint.
Thus its endpoint masses are exactly zero and 1/4, respectively.

I recomputed the unshifted H1 gap:

    U-F1(t)=(136 sqrt(21)-623)/48>11/2400.

Indeed sqrt(21)>1833/400 has square gap 111/160000. On the relevant
threshold interval q>1/4, so the absolute derivative is less than
(18/5-3/2)/(18/25)<3. The threshold displacement is 17/20000.
The resulting remaining deficit is greater than

    11/2400-51/20000=61/30000>1/2000.

For H2 and H3 the exact gaps are
epsilon(4-6t)-3epsilon^2 and 4t epsilon-epsilon^2. Both exceed
epsilon=1/2000 under the displayed rational bounds on t.

Most importantly, the THREE middle caps together with the SIX
endpoint isolates form a fixed finite cover of the ENTIRE S at n=1.
Every member has global raw mass less than (U-epsilon)V. For each
possible center choose a member of that cover containing it; its
depth is at most that member's mass. This proves a strict bound
for the full global maximum, without any inference from a mere
pointwise comparison at the restricted maximizer.

Division by (3/2)V gives the gap (2/3)epsilon=1/3000 exactly.
No factor V remains in the normalized statement.

## 4. The nonfacet local minimum is in the full orientation chart

Near the claimed point all three one-vertex regimes have a strict
positive margin, including in a small beta neighborhood. Expansion
of the two endpoint squares gives precisely the +2 beta^2 term.
Direct differentiation of the numerator
(3/2)a^2-4at+3t^2 and denominator 2a^2-a gives

    F_a=Q(a)/(2a^2-a)^2,
    Q(a)=(8t-3/2)a^2-12t^2 a+3t^2.

The endpoint eliminations are correct. More explicitly the upper
bound t<583/2000 gives Q(17/20)<-23/6250, and the lower bound
t>233/800 gives Q(9/10)>93/10000. The stated derivative lower bound
is positive, so Q has exactly one root in the interval.

At that root, F_aa=Q'/D^2>0, F_beta,beta=4/D>0, and the mixed
derivative is zero. Thus the Hessian is positive definite. Removing
positive normal scaling by u1+u2=1 gives a genuine open chart of ALL
oriented halfspaces through (0,t,t), including variation of the
integer normal. There is no omitted nearby orientation. The continuous
normal (a*,1-a*) is parallel to none of the three triangle facets.
The source claims a strict LOCAL minimum here, which is exactly what
the Hessian proves; it does not confuse this with the separate global
finite-cover argument.

## 5. Extra integer coordinates: both depth directions are exact

At a binary vertex b in the extra n-1 coordinates, put

    q_b(z')=sum_i[(1-b_i)z'_i+b_i(1-z'_i)].

This is affine, zero at b, and at least one at every other binary
vertex. Subtracting a sufficiently large multiple of q_b from any
copy cap's left side excludes all other copies, while preserving
its exact restriction and continuous normal on the chosen copy.
For the nine explicitly displayed caps, coefficient 2 already
suffices: the only potentially larger left-side bound is H3's
value s<3/5, and s-2<-s. The endpoint isolates and the first two
middle caps have still larger exclusion margins.

Conversely, restriction of an ambient containing cap to its own
copy is a containing copy cap, or the entire copy in the harmless
pure-extra-coordinate case mentioned at the beginning. Thus the
raw point depth in the full family is at least the own-copy point
depth. The isolating extension proves the reverse inequality for
every cap and hence for the infimum. This argument works separately
for unrestricted and facet-restricted families, because it never
changes the continuous normal.

There are exactly 2^(n-1) equal copies. Both normalized global bounds
therefore divide by that factor, with no loss depending on n. These
are genuine halfspaces in the original mixed lattice coordinates;
no nonaffine centroid recentering or arbitrary base transformation
is being applied.

## 6. Measure, boundary, and scope audit

Nonvertical cap boundaries have zero H2 mass in every positive triangle.
Saturated/empty endpoint formulas nonetheless use the correct closed
sets. Pure integer caps retain full boundary fibers and were separately
bounded above. The finite covers are closed covers and include their
intersection boundaries.

Continuous invertible linear changes multiply all fiber areas by the
same absolute determinant, and affine base-dependent continuous shears
preserve the lattice and fiber areas. The claimed affine scope is
therefore correct. The proof does not use general position, a width
bound, or a restricted integer tilt.

The ordinary own-middle-fiber lower bound is (4/9)V; dividing by the
total gives 16/(27*2^n)>4/(9*2^n). Thus the example is explicitly
OC-safe. What it disproves is the facet-direction reduction even for
the globally optimized depth; it proves no failure of OC itself.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
